newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Thanksgiving weekend sales up 11.9 pct - ICSC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Thanksgiving weekend sales up 11.9 pct - ICSC.

text.p: Retail sales at shops in U.S. malls for the weekend after Thanskgiving rose 11.9 percent from a year ago on a per square foot basis, the International Council of Shopping Centers said Monday.

The council's survey includes 57 malls with 3,000 shops. Last year, the weekend following Thanksgiving -- the unofficial start of the holiday shopping season -- saw sales flat compared to the prior year, the council said.
The survey does not include department stores or other mall anchor stores.

Apparel sales were up 11.1 percent, footwear up 12.9 percent, jewelry up 15.0 percent, food up 5.7 percent, home furnishings up 14.7 percent, home entertainment up 11.0 percent and cards, gifts and books up 15.1 percent.
Miscellaneous items, which include toys and personal care products, were up 12.0 percent, the council said.
